quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents other vehicles from distracting you.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: What is hardest to see at night?
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than road signs and other objects.

questions.question: After an emergency vehicle with its siren on passes you, what must you do?

options.text: Drive closely behind the emergency vehicle.
Drive as fast as the emergency vehicle.
Stay at least 500 feet behind the emergency vehicle.
Drive very slowly near the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay at least 500 feet behind the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: After an emergency vehicle passes, you must stay at least 500 feet behind it before resuming normal driving.

questions.question: What should you do before starting your vehicle?

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Before starting your vehicle, buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: What should you do after a train passes at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Look for more trains and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for more trains and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: Always check for another train before crossing the tracks, even if there is only one track.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look out the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: Turn your head to see through the rear window when backing up. Mirrors and sensors alone are not enough because children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat.

questions.question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
questions.explanation: A green left arrow means you have the right-of-way. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: What should you do to help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.

questions.explanation: Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn when needed. This helps other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians know what you are doing.

questions.question: What is the penalty for a person under 21 who drinks alcohol but is not driving, for a first offense?

options.text: A 90-day license suspension and up to a $500 fine.

questions.correctAnswerText: A 90-day license suspension and up to a $500 fine.
questions.explanation: The minimum penalty for underage drinking is a fine of up to $500, plus court costs, and a 90-day suspension.

questions.question: What happens to people under 16 who use a fake ID to buy alcohol?

options.text: Their driving is suspended starting on their 16th birthday.
They cannot take the driver's test until age 21.
Their driving is suspended starting on their 21st birthday.
They must take an alcohol safety class.

questions.correctAnswerText: Their driving is suspended starting on their 16th birthday.
questions.explanation: If you are under 21 and convicted of having alcohol, lying about your age, or using a fake ID, your driving will be suspended. If you are under 16, the suspension starts on your 16th birthday.

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle, what distance should you allow?
questions.explanation: On dry pavement, leave at least four seconds of space between you and the vehicle ahead. Always allow extra space when following a motorcycle.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before entering the zone.
You should only reduce your speed to 35 mph in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to reduce their speed. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign mean?

options.text: A reduced speed zone is starting.
You may see more pedestrians ahead.
A reduced speed zone is ending.

questions.correctAnswerText: A reduced speed zone is ending.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times posted. The "End school zone" sign marks the end of a reduced speed zone.

questions.question: This is a ____ sign.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign is a "Yield" sign. Slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and oncoming traffic cross first. Stop only if needed.

questions.question: You must turn on your headlights when you cannot see other vehicles from ____ feet away.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see pedestrians or other vehicles 1,000 feet ahead.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should wave the others ahead.

questions.explanation: All drivers must stop at a four-way stop. The first driver to arrive goes first. If two arrive at the same time, the driver on the right goes first.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians. Sound it when another driver might not see you.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol hurts your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving ability gets worse. Never drink and drive.
